title: AQ Podcast | Daniel Noboa’s Ecuador: Crime, Protests and a Contested Vote
gist: Short podcast teaser: Daniel Noboa, reelected in April 2025 on a security promise and compared to Bukele, still faces entrenched crime (homicides down about 8% in 2026 after a record 2025); Nov. 29 local elections will test him with the main opposition party barred from running under its own name. Guest: Sebastián Hurtado of Prófitas.

themes.theme: Noboa's security record and Nov. 29 electoral test

insights.claim: Ecuador's homicides are down about 8% in 2026 after a record-setting 2025, despite President Daniel Noboa's increasingly aggressive campaign against organized crime and closer ties with the United States.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Only modest crime improvement means Ecuador security risk stays elevated for investors.
insights.quote: Homicides are down about 8% this year after a record-setting 2025

insights.claim: Ecuador's local elections on November 29, 2026 will test Noboa's political strength, with the main opposition party barred from running under its own name and one of its top leaders in jail.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Results are a gauge of Noboa's mandate; opposition exclusion raises democratic-backsliding and protest risk.
insights.quote: with the main opposition party barred from running under its own name, and one of its top leaders in jail

insights.claim: Noboa, reelected in April 2025 on a promise to restore public security, is increasingly compared to El Salvador's Nayib Bukele.
insights.speaker: Americas Quarterly
insights.so_what: Bukele-style governance in Ecuador implies security-first policy with institutional and political risks.
